Subject: Recap: spend corridor & procurement matrix — next steps

Hi Lena / Jamal —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can turn this into a short pilot + procurement path: 

What we heard you say
- Target use case: customer support summarization + private RAG for KB (latency-sensitive, bursty queries).
- Expected steady-state consumption: roughly 200M — 800M tokens/month depending on feature rollout.
- Target unit economics: you indicated an internal target of ~$900 / 1M tokens for production; pilot can be higher.
- Procurement gating: procurement needs a PO threshold and expected lead time to determine whether this goes through self-serve card or PO.

Requests / next steps
1) Can you confirm the monthly budget corridor you want us to model (e.g., $40k–$120k / month)? That helps lock the $/1M token proposals.
2) What is your procurement PO threshold (value above which Procurement requires a formal PO)? Also, what's the average lead time once a PO is submitted?
3) For the pilot, would a 90-day evaluation with a capped trial credit + discounted pilot rates work? We can draft a simple mutual action plan.

I attached a short ballpark estimate (redwood-cost-estimate-1Mtokens.pdf) and a blank PO/threshold template so your procurement team can fill in the gating numbers.

If it helps, I'm available Monday to walk your procurement team through the PO matrix — 30 mins should do it.

Thanks — Ben

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary — that matches our internal notes. A few clarifications from procurement / finance: 

- Confirmed monthly spend corridor for initial sizing: $50k — $140k / month (this covers 250M — 800M tokens depending on compression & caching assumptions).
- Procurement PO threshold: Procurement requires a formal PO for any vendor spend above $75,000 / month. For deals below that we can generally purchase via central card or a short-term contract.
- Typical PO lead time once approved: 4–6 weeks (depends on legal review).

Pilot ask: We can do a 60–90 day pilot. Procurement prefers a capped fixed-credit approach rather than a long-term discounted pilot. If you can provide a $25k pilot credit + 20% pilot discount on usage above credit, Procurement is comfortable moving forward and will prioritize the PO once we decide to commit.

Uploading procurement contact info and a completed PO-threshold snapshot to the Drive link I shared in the call.

On the unit economics, $900 / 1M tokens is within the range we’d accept for production if the latency and reliability SLOs are demonstrated during pilot.

Thanks — Lena

--
Lena Ortiz

Quick internal note after Lena's reply —

Summary:
- Confirmed corridor: $50k–$140k / month (procurement flagged $75k PO threshold).
- Pilot ask: $25k capped credit + 20% off pilot overage.
- Lead time: 4–6 weeks for PO after approval.

Proposed seller options to cover ranges and reduce friction:
1) Pilot package (recommended first step): 90-day sandbox with $25k credit, 20% pilot discount, priority onboarding. Objective: validate latency & token economics.
2) Committed band (3–12 month): tiered $/1M token discounts as commit increases. Example tiers: $1,100 / 1M (base), $950 / 1M (mid commit), $750 / 1M (high commit). These are placeholders; pricing engineering to refine.
3) Enterprise PO path: single monthly invoice with PO, standard 30–60 day payment terms. Procurement prefers PO > $75k.

Next actions for us:
- Marissa: can you prepare a short quote matrix with the three options and modeled spend at 250M / 500M / 800M tokens? Use Lena's corridor to generate per-month and per-1M token pricing.
- Karthik: can you draft a short PO matrix (procurement-PO-thresholds.xlsx) that outlines PO value to approvals/lead-time and sample contract term lengths?
- I'll schedule the procurement walk-through for Monday or Tuesday and share the sandbox link + pilot T&Cs.

I'll keep this thread so external participants see the final quote & PO matrix.

Ben
